fatal_errors: The proposed friction stir processing intervention does not reconstruct the SPS-fabricated HEA electrodes and electrospark-deposited multilayer coating intervention.
Friction stir processing alone redistributes existing material and may not restore material or geometry lost from a damaged component.
The hypothesis predicts performance under high-temperature, fatigue, and corrosive service without material-specific evidence or supporting citations.
It omits the target compositions, C1018 substrate, SPS processing windows, ESD parameters, and three-versus-six-layer comparison.
The target study did not test aggressive-environment, corrosion, fatigue, or service performance, so the claimed benefits exceed the available evidence.
explanation: The response addresses the general motivation of avoiding fusion-related hot cracking and gives a reasonably discriminating comparison experiment. Its solid-state deformation mechanism is scientifically plausible in suitable, tool-accessible and plastically processable alloys. However, it is not a reconstruction of the target, which used high-temperature SPS to consolidate mechanically alloyed CrFeNiMo-family powders into electrodes followed by electrospark deposition on C1018 steel. The relevant target outcomes were densification, porosity, hardness, coating continuity, oxidation, roughness, microfissuring, and the useful six-layer limit—not demonstrated superiority to fusion welding under aggressive service. The absence of cited evidence, material identity, process parameters, geometry-restoration strategy, and validated environmental boundaries makes the proposed alternative unsupported despite its testable experimental outline.
